title: Ragtime, dances and Piron's band at society parties
summary: Raised on opera and ragtime, she danced to Celestin, Piron and other bands at fraternity dances, debut parties and the Country Club, where Piron called on guests to perform.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: When did you first come aware of the festival and the jazz?

Well, I first heard Ragtime, and I was very aware of music and was brought up in an atmosphere of music, taken to the opera very early in life, and we had all sorts of music. Naturally, when Ragtime came in, my father had that too. And I could remember the turkey trots and things like that. And then later on, when I was about 15 and 16 and started going to the fraternity dances, they had the Celestans Band, Piran, and all the good Dixieland jazz bands of the city. Gradually, as we grew up, in the debut parties and all the parties that I ever went to in New Orleans, we danced to jazz music.

Oh, yes. And private parties and other private parties, Tate-en-sons. The New Orleans Country Club had Tate-en-sons on Saturdays and Sundays, where they had the famous Perron himself. And he knew all of our crowd and the ones that were gifted and could dance and sing. And at all the parties, he would act as a sort of massive ceremonies and call on us to get up and do our stuff. We'd sing, harmonize, dance. You really don't see the young people do that as much as we used to, because that was a golden age of jazz. And we danced every night, you know, and in the daytime. We danced, I feel, more than the generations danced today.
